newsitem.title: UK: Business slacker at end-week on sugar freight mkt.
newsitem.headline: Business slacker at end-week on sugar freight mkt.

text.p: Business was thin on the ground on London's sugar freight market at the end of the week with only a handful of fixtures and orders reported, shipobrokers said on Friday.
Cargill quoted for 15,600/16,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Venezuela for prompt shipment.
Louis Dreyfus issued two new bulk orders for US Gulf/Atlantic, both for mid-June dates. It quoted for 20,000 tonnes from Durban and another similar cargo from the Philippines.

Shipbrokers said the only firmer business reported on Friday came from Sugar Chartering, which fixed 19/21,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Recife to US Gulf/Atlanitc. The freight rate and shipment date were unclear, they said.
In other news, Iraq has agreed to buy 37,500 tonnes of sugar from Egypt although the contract still has to be approved by the United Nations.

The Philippines plans to import between 300,000 and 350,000 tonnes of sugar for 1997/98 (Sept/Aug) for buffer stocks and will maintain a 65 percent tariff on refined sugar imported from neighbouring countries.
Pakistan on Friday cancelled its tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of white refined crystal sugar for delivery at Karachi port or nearby Port Qasim by July 31.
